newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila banks focus on one-year T-bills.
newsitem.headline: Manila banks focus on one-year T-bills.

text.p: Manila banks began scrambling for one-year Treasury bills after the government announced it would cut down on its offer of long-term bills and offer more short tenors, dealers said.
The Bureau of Treasury said it decided to cut the volume of one-year T-bills next week to 500 million pesos from two billion pesos because of the prevailing high interest rates.
"That spurred demand for the one-year bills. But no one wanted to sell," a dealer said.
The demand prompted banks to lower their quotes for the one-year bills, traders said.

A Reuters poll of five financial institutions gave lower bids of 15/16 percent and offer rates of 14.25/14.50 percent. Banks quoted on Wednesday bids of 15.50/16 percent and offers of 14.5/15 percent.
The average interbank call loan rate fell to 28.1875 percent from 32.1875 percent in reaction to the four percentage-point cut in the central bank's overnight borrowing rate to 28 percent.
Volume increased to 12.66 billion pesos from 13.01 billion. The market had 29 lenders out of the 41 participating financial institutions.
